title: Ad Detective: Crack the Marketing Code
description: You're running a stall at your school's Market Day! Over 10 weeks, learn how to find your audience, build a brand, set prices, create ads, and market ethically. Every choice shapes your stall's success — can you crack the marketing code?
how_to_play: You manage a school Market Day stall over 10 exciting weeks.
Each round is a marketing challenge — choose wisely to grow your brand!
Watch your dashboard: Brand Awareness, Customer Satisfaction, Sales, and more are all connected.
Random events like viral posts and rainy days will test your adaptability.
NPCs like Ms. Marketing, Competitor Kid, and Customer Chloe react to your decisions.
Balance creativity, ethics, and profit — the best marketers do all three!
learning_objectives: Understand what marketing is and why businesses need it
Learn to identify a target audience and tailor messages
Practice branding, pricing, and advertising decisions
Recognize persuasion techniques and ethical boundaries
Develop creative thinking for campaigns and promotions
Build empathy by understanding customer needs
cultural_context: School market day, youth entrepreneurship, responsible advertising, global classroom setting

tick_rules.label: Weekly Sales
tick_rules.description: Your stall earns money each week based on brand awareness and customer satisfaction.

tick_rules.label: Weekly Stall Costs
tick_rules.description: Running a stall costs a small amount each week for supplies.

tick_rules.label: Learning by Doing
tick_rules.description: You learn a little more about marketing each week.

tick_rules.label: Word of Mouth
tick_rules.description: Happy customers tell their friends about your stall.

interactions.label: Brand Recognition
interactions.description: Strong brands attract more buyers and boost sales.

interactions.label: Trust Through Honesty
interactions.description: Ethical marketing builds long-term customer trust.

interactions.label: Reputation Risk
interactions.description: Shady marketing damages your brand reputation.

interactions.label: Creative Edge
interactions.description: Creative campaigns make your stall memorable.

random_events.label: Viral Social Media Post
random_events.description: A classmate posted a photo of your stall on social media and it went viral! Everyone is talking about your products.
random_events.news_text: TRENDING: Your stall is going viral! Classmates are sharing photos and tagging friends.
random_events.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon school kids excitedly looking at a phone showing a viral post about a market stall, colorful social media icons floating, bright cheerful school setting

random_events.label: Copycat Competitor
random_events.description: Competitor Kid has copied your best-selling product idea! Customers are confused about which stall is the original.
random_events.news_text: ALERT: Competitor Kid is selling a copycat version of your product! Customers can't tell the difference.
random_events.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon school market day, two similar-looking stalls side by side, one kid looking annoyed while another kid copies their sign, confused customers in between

random_events.label: School Newspaper Feature
random_events.description: The school newspaper wants to write a feature article about your stall! Great free publicity.
random_events.news_text: FEATURED: The school newspaper runs a full-page story about your amazing stall!
random_events.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon school newspaper with headline about a student market stall, kids reading excitedly, colorful school hallway, bulletin board

random_events.label: Rain on Market Day
random_events.description: It's pouring rain on Market Day! Fewer customers are showing up, and your outdoor display is getting wet.
random_events.news_text: WEATHER: Rain soaks the market! Stalls scramble to protect their goods. Footfall drops sharply.
random_events.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon rainy school courtyard, kids with umbrellas, a market stall with wet products, puddles, grey sky but colorful stalls trying to stay cheerful

behaviors.message: Impressive! You're really starting to think like a marketer. Keep applying what you've learned!
I'm concerned about some of your marketing practices. Remember — good marketing is honest marketing!
Your brand isn't getting noticed. Think about what makes your stall special and tell people about it!
You've truly cracked the marketing code — smart, creative, AND ethical. I'm nominating you for the Young Marketer Award!
Your stall is doing better than mine?! I'll just lower my prices until you can't compete!
Ha! Nobody even knows your stall exists. Maybe you should give up and just buy from mine!
Competitor Kid slashes all prices to steal your customers! It's an all-out price war!
I LOVE your stall! I'm telling all my friends to come buy from you. You really listen to what we want!
Your products aren't what I expected from the ads. I feel a bit misled. My friends feel the same.
Wow, your stall looks so cool and different! I keep coming back just to see what's new.

news_templates.text: Market Day Star! Your stall has earned over {sales_revenue} coins this season!
Your stall is the talk of the school — famous AND trusted!

simulation_config.ai_scene_prompt_template: A cheerful cartoon school market day scene. A colorful stall run by an 11-year-old student entrepreneur. Brand awareness {brand_awareness}%, customer satisfaction {customer_satisfaction}%, creativity {creativity}%. Mood: {'bustling and exciting' if customer_satisfaction > 60 else 'quiet and struggling' if customer_satisfaction < 30 else 'steady and hopeful'}. Bright colors, school courtyard, other kids as customers.

rounds.situation: It's your first week planning your Market Day stall! Before you sell anything, you need to figure out WHO you're selling to. Your school has younger kids (ages 6-8), your classmates (ages 11-12), teachers, and visiting parents. You can't please everyone — so who's your target audience?
rounds.goal: Choose your target audience and understand their needs.
rounds.coaching_moment: Target audience: The first rule of marketing is knowing WHO you're talking to. Different people want different things.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why is it better to focus on one group of customers instead of trying to sell to everyone?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon school courtyard, diverse group of kids, teachers, and parents walking around, one student with a notebook observing them, thought bubbles showing different customer types, bright cheerful style

choices.label: A. Target Your Classmates
choices.description: Focus on 11-12 year olds — you know exactly what they like because you ARE one of them!
choices.feedback: Smart choice! Marketing to people you understand well is a strong strategy. You know their tastes, their language, and their budget.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.

choices.label: B. Target Younger Kids
choices.description: The 6-8 year olds have pocket money and love fun, colorful things. Easy to impress!
choices.feedback: Younger kids are enthusiastic buyers, but marketing to very young children raises ethical questions. Are they old enough to make smart buying decisions?

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.

choices.label: C. Try to Sell to Everyone
choices.description: Why pick one group? Cast a wide net — kids, teachers, parents, everyone!
choices.feedback: Trying to please everyone often means pleasing no one. Your message becomes vague and your stall loses its identity. This is a common beginner mistake!

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

choices.label: D. Target Visiting Parents
choices.description: Parents have more money and appreciate quality. Premium audience!
choices.feedback: Interesting niche! Parents do spend more, but they visit less often. You'll need premium products and a professional look.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.

rounds.situation: You need a brand identity — a name, logo, and vibe that makes your stall instantly recognizable. Ms. Marketing says: 'A brand is a promise to your customer. What do you want to be known for?' You have a few ideas...
rounds.goal: Create a brand identity for your stall.
rounds.coaching_moment: Branding: A brand isn't just a logo — it's the feeling customers get when they think of you. Consistency is key.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Think of your favorite brand. What makes it stick in your mind? Is it the logo, the colors, or how it makes you feel?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon student at a desk designing a brand logo with colored markers, sketches of different logos and slogans pinned on a board, creative workshop feel, bright and fun

choices.label: A. Fun & Playful Brand
choices.description: Bright colors, silly name, mascot character. 'The Snack Shack' with a cartoon mascot!
choices.feedback: A fun brand is memorable and approachable! Your mascot gives customers something to connect with emotionally.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.

choices.label: B. Premium & Professional Brand
choices.description: Clean design, sophisticated name, quality packaging. 'The Artisan Corner' with elegant fonts.
choices.feedback: A premium brand lets you charge higher prices. Customers expect quality, so you must deliver on that promise!

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

choices.label: C. Eco-Friendly Brand
choices.description: Recycled materials, green colors, nature theme. 'Green Goodies' with a leaf logo.
choices.feedback: An eco-brand attracts socially conscious customers. But remember — you must actually BE eco-friendly, not just look green!

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.
skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.

choices.label: D. Skip Branding — Just Sell Stuff
choices.description: Why waste time on logos? Just put products on the table and let them speak for themselves.
choices.feedback: Without a brand, customers walk right past your stall. In a crowded market, being invisible is the biggest risk of all.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

rounds.situation: Time to set prices! Your products cost about 10 coins each to make. Competitor Kid charges 15 coins for similar items. You need to decide: go cheap to attract crowds, match the competition, or charge more for your unique brand? Ms. Marketing reminds you: 'Price sends a message about quality.'
rounds.goal: Set a pricing strategy that fits your brand and market.
rounds.coaching_moment: Pricing psychology: Price isn't just about cost — it's a signal. Low prices say 'bargain,' high prices say 'premium.' What message do you want to send?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why do some people pay more for a branded product when a cheaper one does the same thing?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon student looking at a chalkboard with different price tags and coins, thinking hard, math symbols floating around, a market stall in the background, bright school setting

choices.label: A. Bargain Prices (12 coins)
choices.description: Undercut everyone! Sell cheap and make it up with volume. Everyone loves a deal.
choices.feedback: Low prices attract crowds, but thin margins mean you need to sell A LOT to make money. Also, customers may think 'cheap price = cheap quality.'

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.

choices.label: B. Match the Competition (15 coins)
choices.description: Same price as Competitor Kid. Win on quality and service, not price.
choices.feedback: Matching the competition is safe. Now you need another way to stand out — better service, better product, or better branding.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

choices.label: C. Premium Pricing (22 coins)
choices.description: Charge more because your brand is worth it. Fewer sales, but higher profit per item.
choices.feedback: Premium pricing works IF your brand supports it. Customers expect premium quality for premium prices. Deliver on your promise!

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.

choices.label: D. Special Deals & Bundles
choices.description: Create combo packs and 'Buy 2, Get 1 Free' offers. Make pricing fun!
choices.feedback: Bundles increase how much each customer spends! Smart marketers know that a 'deal' makes customers feel like they're winning.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.

rounds.situation: Your stall is set up, but people need to KNOW about it! It's time for your first advertising campaign. You have a limited budget and need to choose where to spend it. Posters? Announcements? Social media? Or something totally creative?
rounds.goal: Launch your first advertising campaign to attract customers.
rounds.coaching_moment: Advertising: The best ads don't just inform — they make people FEEL something. What emotion will your ad trigger?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Think about an ad you've seen recently. What made you remember it? Was it funny, surprising, or emotional?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon student putting up colorful handmade posters in a school hallway, other kids stopping to look, megaphone and social media icons, creative ad campaign feel

choices.label: A. Poster Blitz
choices.description: Design 20 eye-catching posters and put them EVERYWHERE — hallways, bathrooms, cafeteria!
choices.feedback: Posters are classic advertising! Repetition builds recognition. The more people see your brand, the more they remember it.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

choices.label: B. Social Media Campaign
choices.description: Create an Instagram page for your stall with behind-the-scenes content and polls.
choices.feedback: Social media lets customers interact with your brand! Polls and behind-the-scenes content make people feel involved.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.

choices.label: C. Word-of-Mouth Squad
choices.description: Give free samples to popular kids and ask them to spread the word. Influencer marketing!
choices.feedback: People trust recommendations from friends more than any ad! But is it honest if 'influencers' don't say they got free stuff?

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.

choices.label: D. Attention-Grabbing Stunt
choices.description: Do something wild! A flash mob at lunch, a mystery box challenge, or a live product demo.
choices.feedback: Stunts create buzz! They're risky — if it works, you're famous; if it flops, you're embarrassed. High risk, high reward.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.

rounds.situation: Ms. Marketing teaches the class about persuasion techniques used in real advertising. She shows examples: emotional appeals, celebrity endorsements, scarcity ('Only 5 left!'), and social proof ('Everyone's buying this!'). Now she asks: how will YOU persuade customers?
rounds.goal: Choose a persuasion technique for your marketing.
rounds.coaching_moment: Persuasion: Understanding how ads influence people helps you be both a better marketer AND a smarter consumer. Not all persuasion is ethical.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is it okay to make people WANT something they don't need? Where's the line between persuasion and manipulation?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon classroom scene, teacher showing a whiteboard with persuasion techniques illustrated, lightbulbs going off over students' heads, colorful examples of ads

choices.label: A. Emotional Storytelling
choices.description: Tell the story behind your products — who made them, why they matter, how they help. Make customers FEEL.
choices.feedback: Stories connect people to products on an emotional level. When the story is TRUE, it's the most powerful and ethical form of persuasion.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.

choices.label: B. Scarcity & Urgency
choices.description: Put up signs: 'Limited edition!' and 'Only 10 left — going fast!' Create FOMO!
choices.feedback: Scarcity makes people act fast! But if you FAKE scarcity (you actually have plenty), that's deceptive. Customers who find out will feel tricked.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

choices.label: C. Social Proof & Reviews
choices.description: Display customer reviews, a 'Most Popular' board, and a live sales counter. Show that everyone's buying!
choices.feedback: People follow the crowd! Real reviews build trust. Just make sure the reviews are genuine — fake reviews destroy credibility.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.

choices.label: D. Free Samples & Try Before You Buy
choices.description: Let everyone try a small free sample. If they like it, they'll buy the full version.
choices.feedback: Free samples are the ultimate honest marketing! You're saying: 'Our product is so good, we'll let you try it for free.' Confidence!

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.

rounds.situation: Competitor Kid has started an all-out price war! He's slashing prices on everything, even selling some items below cost just to steal your customers. Other stalls are panicking and dropping their prices too. Your sales are plummeting. The whole market is in chaos. What do you do?
rounds.goal: Survive the price war without destroying your brand or going broke.
rounds.coaching_moment: Resilience in competition: Price wars hurt EVERYONE. The smartest businesses find ways to compete on value, not just price. Sometimes the best move is to NOT play the price game.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When a competitor drops their prices, is matching them always the right response? What else can you compete on?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon school market day in chaos, two rival stalls with competing price signs getting lower and lower, worried student stallholders, coins flying, dramatic cartoon style

choices.label: A. Match Their Low Prices
choices.description: Drop your prices even lower! If they go to 8 coins, you go to 7. Win the price war!
choices.feedback: You won the price war but lost money on every sale. Both stalls are now barely surviving. Nobody wins a race to the bottom.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.

choices.label: B. Add Value, Not Discounts
choices.description: Keep your prices steady but add extras — gift wrapping, personalized notes, loyalty stamps.
choices.feedback: Brilliant! You competed on VALUE, not price. Customers choose you because you offer a better EXPERIENCE, not just a cheaper product.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.

choices.label: C. Propose a Truce
choices.description: Talk to Competitor Kid and suggest you both stop the price war. Maybe even collaborate on a joint deal!
choices.feedback: Cooperation over competition! In real business, partnerships often beat rivalries. You turned a competitor into a collaborator.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

choices.label: D. Pivot Your Product Completely
choices.description: If they're copying your products, sell something COMPLETELY different that they can't copy.
choices.feedback: A bold pivot! Reinventing your offering escapes the price war entirely. Innovation is the best competitive advantage.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.

rounds.situation: You've been selling for a few weeks now. Customer Chloe tells you: 'Some kids love your stall, but others say it's not what they expected.' It's time to collect feedback and really listen. Ms. Marketing says: 'The best marketers are the best listeners.'
rounds.goal: Gather customer feedback and decide how to respond.
rounds.coaching_moment: Customer feedback: Marketing isn't just talking AT customers — it's listening TO them. Feedback is a gift, even when it's negative.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why is negative feedback sometimes more valuable than positive feedback?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon student with a clipboard interviewing other kids at a school market, speech bubbles with stars and suggestions, colorful feedback forms, friendly atmosphere

choices.label: A. Detailed Customer Survey
choices.description: Create a fun survey with prizes for completing it. Ask what they like, dislike, and want more of.
choices.feedback: Surveys give you DATA, not just opinions. Smart marketers make decisions based on what customers actually say, not what they assume.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.

choices.label: B. Anonymous Suggestion Box
choices.description: Put out a suggestion box so people can share honest opinions without feeling awkward.
choices.feedback: Anonymous feedback is often the most honest. People say what they really think when they don't fear judgment. Brave choice!

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.

choices.label: C. Ignore the Critics
choices.description: You can't please everyone! Focus on the customers who already love you and ignore the haters.
choices.feedback: Ignoring feedback is a dangerous game. Today's critics could have been tomorrow's loyal customers — if you'd just listened.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

choices.label: D. Customer Focus Group
choices.description: Invite 5 customers to a 'taste test' session where they try new products and give live feedback.
choices.feedback: Focus groups give you deep insights you can't get from surveys. Watching customers react in real-time is incredibly valuable!

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.

rounds.situation: Disaster! A rumor is spreading that your stall has been using misleading advertising. Someone posted a comparison of your ads vs. reality, and it's going viral in the school chat groups. Whether it's true or exaggerated, your reputation is on the line. Customer Chloe says: 'Everyone's talking about it. You need to respond.'
rounds.goal: Handle the brand crisis and rebuild trust before it's too late.
rounds.coaching_moment: Ethical marketing: Trust takes years to build and seconds to destroy. How you respond to a crisis defines your brand more than any ad campaign.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When a brand makes a mistake, would you rather they deny it, ignore it, or admit it and fix it? Why?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon student looking worried at a phone showing angry messages, school hallway with other kids whispering, a stall with a 'closed temporarily' sign, dramatic cartoon style

choices.label: A. Public Apology & Transparency
choices.description: Post an honest apology, explain what happened, and promise to change. Full transparency.
choices.feedback: Incredible courage! Honest apologies are powerful. Customers respect brands that own their mistakes. Trust is being rebuilt.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.

choices.label: B. Deny Everything
choices.description: It's not true! Fight back, say the rumor is fake, and blame Competitor Kid for spreading lies.
choices.feedback: Denial usually makes things worse. If evidence surfaces later, you'll lose ALL credibility. The cover-up is always worse than the crime.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.

choices.label: C. Rebrand and Start Fresh
choices.description: Change your stall name, logo, and products. Basically start over with a clean slate.
choices.feedback: A total rebrand is expensive and risky. You lose everything you built. Sometimes it's better to fix the problem than run from it.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: D. Actions Speak Louder — Quality Upgrade
choices.description: Don't just say sorry — SHOW it. Upgrade your products, offer refunds, and over-deliver on quality.
choices.feedback: Actions beat words! By actually improving your product, you prove your commitment to customers. This is how lasting trust is built.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

rounds.situation: Ms. Marketing shows the class some real ads that were banned for being misleading: a cereal ad that said 'makes you taller,' a toy ad that showed impossible stunts, and a snack ad that hid the unhealthy ingredients. She asks your team to create marketing guidelines for Market Day. What rules matter most?
rounds.goal: Create ethical marketing guidelines for your stall.
rounds.coaching_moment: Ethical reasoning: Good marketing tells the truth in an interesting way. Bad marketing tells lies in a convincing way. Both can sell products — but only one builds lasting success.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Should ads be allowed to exaggerate? Where is the line between 'creative storytelling' and 'lying'?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon classroom with students debating, examples of good and bad ads on screen, teacher moderating, scales of justice symbol, thought-provoking colorful scene

choices.label: A. Strict Honesty Policy
choices.description: Every claim must be 100% true and provable. No exaggeration allowed. 'If we can't prove it, we don't say it.'
choices.feedback: Radical honesty! It might limit your creative freedom, but customers will trust every word you say. That trust is priceless.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.

choices.label: B. Balanced Guidelines
choices.description: Be honest about important stuff (ingredients, safety), but creative language ('World's Tastiest!') is fine.
choices.feedback: A practical balance! Most real companies follow this approach. The key is: never mislead about anything that affects the customer's decision.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.

choices.label: C. Creative Freedom — No Limits
choices.description: Marketing IS exaggeration! Let creativity run wild. 'Nobody takes ads literally anyway.'
choices.feedback: Unethical! 'Everyone does it' doesn't make it right. Misleading ads might boost short-term sales, but they destroy long-term trust.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.

choices.label: D. Let Customers Set the Rules
choices.description: Ask Customer Chloe and other buyers what marketing practices they'd find unfair. Let the audience decide.
choices.feedback: Involving customers in rule-setting is incredibly smart! They feel respected, and you learn exactly what they consider fair.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.

rounds.situation: The school is launching an online marketplace where stalls can sell digitally too! It's a whole new channel. Ms. Marketing says: 'Digital marketing is where the future is — but it comes with new rules and new risks.' Do you go all-in online, or keep things physical?
rounds.coaching_moment: Digital marketing: Online channels amplify everything — good reviews spread fast, but so do bad ones. Your digital presence must be authentic.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How is advertising to someone online different from advertising to someone in person? Which is more honest?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon student at a computer designing an online store, website mockup on screen, social media icons floating around, split scene showing physical stall and digital shop, bright tech-meets-school vibe

choices.label: A. Go All-In Digital
choices.description: Move everything online! Build a website, run social ads, start an email newsletter.
choices.feedback: Going digital expands your reach enormously! But you might lose the personal touch that makes a school market special.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.

choices.label: B. Hybrid Approach
choices.description: Keep your physical stall but add an online ordering page. Best of both worlds.
choices.feedback: Hybrid is the smart play! You keep the personal connection while reaching customers who can't visit in person.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

choices.label: C. Stay Physical Only
choices.description: Your stall's charm is the face-to-face experience. Digital would dilute it. Keep it real!
choices.feedback: There's something powerful about sticking to your strengths. But refusing to adapt can leave you behind as others go digital.

skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.
skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.

choices.label: D. Become a Content Creator
choices.description: Start a YouTube channel about your Market Day journey — behind-the-scenes, tutorials, taste tests!
choices.feedback: Content marketing is incredibly powerful! By sharing your journey, you build a community, not just a customer base.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.

rounds.situation: Market Day Finals are next week! This is your last chance to launch a major campaign. You've got marketing knowledge, a brand, and a team. Ms. Marketing says: 'Everything you've learned comes together NOW.' Competitor Kid is planning something big too. What's your grand finale campaign?
rounds.goal: Launch your biggest marketing campaign yet.
rounds.coaching_moment: Campaign strategy: A great campaign combines audience understanding, branding, creativity, and ethics into one unified message. This is where all your skills come together.
rounds.reflection_prompt: If you could only tell customers ONE thing about your stall, what would it be and why?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon student leading a team making a big campaign plan, storyboards and designs on the wall, countdown calendar showing 'Market Day Finals', energy and excitement, colorful war room

choices.label: A. Emotional 'Our Story' Campaign
choices.description: Tell the story of your stall from Week 1 to now — the struggles, the growth, the friendships. Make people root for you.
choices.feedback: Storytelling is the oldest and most powerful form of marketing. Your authentic journey inspires customers to support you.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.

choices.label: B. Viral Challenge Campaign
choices.description: Create a fun challenge (like a taste test or brand quiz) that spreads through the school. Go viral!
choices.feedback: Viral campaigns explode your reach! But virality is unpredictable — you might go viral for the wrong reasons too.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

choices.label: C. Customer Loyalty Rewards
choices.description: Launch a loyalty card: buy 5, get 1 free. Plus VIP early access for your biggest fans.
choices.feedback: Loyalty programs turn one-time buyers into repeat customers! It costs less to keep a customer than to find a new one.

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.

choices.label: D. Collaboration Campaign
choices.description: Partner with another stall for a joint product and cross-promote to both audiences. Double the reach!
choices.feedback: Collaboration beats competition! Cross-promotion doubles your audience at half the cost. Smart marketers build bridges.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.

rounds.situation: Market Day Finals are here! Your stall has grown from nothing into a real brand. Ms. Marketing asks you one final question: 'What do you want people to remember about your stall?' This is your legacy decision — it defines what kind of marketer you are.
rounds.goal: Define your marketing legacy and what your brand stands for.
rounds.coaching_moment: Legacy: The best brands leave a positive mark on the world. Marketing is a powerful tool — you choose whether to use it for good.
rounds.reflection_prompt: If you started a real business someday, what values from this experience would you carry with you?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Cartoon grand school Market Day finale, decorated stalls, banners, judges, excited students and parents, trophy on display, golden light, celebration atmosphere

choices.label: A. Donate Profits to Charity
choices.description: Announce that 50% of today's profits go to a school charity. Marketing with purpose!
choices.feedback: Purpose-driven marketing! Customers love supporting businesses that give back. You proved that doing good IS good business.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.

choices.label: B. Teach Others What You Learned
choices.description: Create a 'Marketing 101' guide for next year's students. Pass on your knowledge!
choices.feedback: Teaching is the highest form of understanding! Your guide will help future students start ahead. Knowledge shared is knowledge multiplied.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.

choices.label: C. Go All-Out for Maximum Profit
choices.description: This is it — flash sales, upsells, last-chance offers! Make every coin you can!
choices.feedback: Maximum profit! But at what cost? Aggressive last-day tactics can leave a bad final impression. Is this the memory you want?

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

choices.label: D. Create an Experience, Not Just a Stall
choices.description: Transform your stall into an immersive experience — music, decorations, photo booth, live demonstrations!
choices.feedback: You created a MEMORY, not just a transaction! Experience marketing is the future — people forget products but remember experiences.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.

glossary_terms.definition: The specific group of people a business aims its products and marketing messages at, based on their age, interests, needs, or habits.
The visible elements of a brand — name, logo, colors, and style — that together create a recognizable image in customers' minds.
The method a business uses to set prices for its products, considering costs, competition, customer willingness to pay, and brand positioning.
Methods used in advertising to influence people's decisions, such as emotional appeals, scarcity ('limited time!'), and social proof ('everyone's buying it!').
Marketing that is honest, transparent, and fair — it doesn't mislead customers or exploit vulnerable groups like young children.
A psychological principle where people follow the actions of others, assuming that if many people are doing something, it must be good.
When customers repeatedly choose one brand over others because of positive experiences, trust, and emotional connection.
Promoting products or services through digital channels like social media, websites, email, and online ads to reach a wider audience.

endings.title: Marketing Genius
endings.message: You did it all — built an amazing brand, kept customers happy, made a profit, AND stayed ethical! Ms. Marketing is speechless. You've won the Young Marketer of the Year award! You proved that smart, creative, honest marketing is the most powerful kind of all. The marketing world better watch out — a genius is coming!

endings.title: Brand Builder
endings.message: Your stall became the most recognized brand at Market Day! Even kids who didn't buy anything know your name, your logo, and your slogan. You've learned that branding isn't just about selling — it's about creating an identity that people connect with. Future brand manager in the making!

endings.title: Customer Champion
endings.message: Your customers LOVE you! Customer Chloe calls your stall 'the best thing about school.' You didn't just sell products — you built relationships, listened to feedback, and made people feel valued. In marketing, nothing beats genuine customer love. You've got what money can't buy: trust.

endings.title: Ethical Marketer
endings.message: Ms. Marketing holds up your stall as the gold standard for ethical marketing. You never lied, never manipulated, and still ran a successful business. You proved that honesty and success aren't opposites — they're partners. The school adopts your marketing guidelines for ALL future Market Days!

endings.title: Market Learner
endings.message: Your stall had its ups and downs, but you know what? You LEARNED. You learned about branding, pricing, advertising, customer feedback, and ethics. Not every campaign worked, but every mistake taught you something. Ms. Marketing smiles: 'The best marketers never stop learning.' Your journey is just beginning!

choices.text: Listen to the team and consider different views

questions.explanation: Good leaders listen to diverse perspectives before making informed decisions.

questions.question: What does 'delayed gratification' mean?

choices.text: Waiting for a bigger reward instead of taking a smaller one now

questions.explanation: Delayed gratification means resisting a smaller immediate reward for a larger future one.
